author: blackstraysheep
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/blackstraysheep/Kuawase/security/code-scanning/27](https://github.com/blackstraysheep/Kuawase/security/code-scanning/27)

In general, the fix is to tighten validation of user-controlled values before using them as stylesheet `href`s, and to ensure that untrusted `message` events cannot directly control which CSS file gets loaded. This means removing or constraining support for arbitrary `file://` and `css/` URLs from untrusted sources, and only allowing a small, strictly validated set of theme identifiers or filenames.

The best targeted fix here without changing existing intended behavior more than necessary is:
- Make `sanitizeCssThemeValue` stricter for “direct” URLs:
  - Remove support for `file://` entirely (so untrusted messages can’t choose arbitrary filesystem paths).
  - For values starting with `css/`, ensure the remainder is a simple filename matching `/^[\w.-]+\.css$/` and reject anything else.
- Leave the `builtin` and `user:` branches unchanged, since they already require a safe filename pattern and/or are further constrained by the Electron main process.

With these changes:
- A `message` carrying `css-theme` can only cause:
  - A built-in theme under `css/` with a validated filename, or
  - A “user” theme that gets resolved server-side/main-process-side to a safe path.
- An attacker can no longer inject arbitrary URLs or `file://` paths into the `href` attribute.

All edits are confined to `js/common-theme.js`, specifically the `isDirectCssHref` and `sanitizeCssThemeValue` functions.

body:
Fixes #367

## Summary

- `registerMermaidAddons()` in `src/markdownPreview/index.ts` is `async` but was not being `await`ed, causing a race condition where `renderMermaidBlocksInElement()` could fire before mermaid's built-in diagram type detectors were registered
- This resulted in "No diagram type detected matching given configuration for text:" on initial markdown preview load
- The notebook entry point (`src/notebook/index.ts:25`) already correctly `await`s this call — this PR aligns the markdown preview entry point

## Change

One-line fix: `registerMermaidAddons()` → `await registerMermaidAddons()`

## Test

1. Open a markdown file with a mermaid diagram
2. Open the markdown preview
3. Diagram should render correctly on first load (no longer requires an edit to trigger re-render)

author: michael-genson
body: ## What this PR does / why we need it: _(REQUIRED)_ Follow up to https://github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie/pull/6984 which enabled query filters using relative dates. This adds limited support to the UI. There's a new internal `FieldType` of `relativeDate`. Currently only `last_made` uses this field type. This is what the UI looks like: Where your only two operators are: "days ago" is translatable, and supports zero/one/multiple (i.e. `1 day ago`): This was added to both meal plan rules and the recipe finder. I didn't add this to cookbooks because I don't think it makes sense for cookbooks to be dynamic. There are several intentional limitations of this UI: - Only "negative" displacements are supported (e.g. you cannot set a value of "30 days in the future"; you can _only_ set X days ago, including "0 days ago") - Only intervals of days are supported (so if you want to do months/years you must convert to days. You cannot do hours/minutes/seconds) - "older than" includes the day (e.g. "older than 30 days" translates to `date <= $NOW-30d`) - "newer than" _also_ includes the day (e.g. "newer than 30 days" translates to `date >= $NOW-30d`) - Fields configured as relative dates _cannot_ use absolute dates, and vice versa (e.g. `created_at` can _only_ reference an _absolute_ date; `last_made` can _only_ reference a _relative_ date) I tried to support a few more configurations but implementation of this got extremely complicated, so I came up with a simpler approach (which is still kind of complicated under the hood but the UX is _very_ simple). The complexity of the UX was not at all worth the added value of slightly more configuration when 99.99% of users aren't going to care. Users always have the option of setting custom queries via the backend if they really want to. ## Which issue(s) this PR fixes: _(REQUIRED)_ N/A ## Special notes for your reviewer: _(fill-in or delete this section)_ Would love some feedback on whether or not this implementation is intuitive. I think it is, but I wrote it 😄 I also made a few layout tweaks to support larger queries. Not really relevant for the new feature, but it was helpful during development and I think it's a marginal improvement so I left it in. ## Testing _(fill-in or delete this section)_ Created simple Meal Plan rules which were properly respected, including compound queries with multiple date rules. This is mostly taken care of in [the backend PR](https://github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie/pull/6984), though.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization (org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-serialization-bom)</summary>

### [`v1.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1110--2026-04-10)

\==================

This release is based on Kotlin 2.3.20 and provides new Json exceptions API and some bugfixes and improvements.

#### Expose Json exceptions structure

To make working with exceptions easier and providing proper error codes in e.g., REST APIs,
classes `JsonException`, `JsonDecodingException`, and `JsonEncodingException` are now public.
They have relevant public properties, such as `shortMessage`, `path`, `offset`, and others.
This API is currently experimental, and we're going to improve it further in the subsequent releases.
See the linked issues for the details: [#​1930](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/1930), [#​1877](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/1877).

#### Ability to hide user input from exception messages for security/privacy reasons.

Historically, exception messages in kotlinx.serialization often included the input Json itself for debuggability reason.
Such behavior may pose additional challenges for logging, analytics, and other systems, since
a system is not always allowed to store user data due to privacy/security reasons, which imposes additional sanitation logic.
To address this issue, a new property `exceptionsWithDebugInfo` is added to `JsonConfiguration`.
Disable it to hide user input from exception messages.
IMPORTANT: This behavior will be enabled by default when this property becomes stable.
See [#​2590](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/2590) for more details.

#### Bugfixes and improvements

- CBOR: Relax value range check when decoding numbers ([#​3167](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3167))
- Use a specialized writeDecimalLong method for IO stream integrations in Json ([#​3152](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3152))

### [`v1.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1100--2026-01-21)

\==================

This release is based on Kotlin 2.3.0 and contains all of the changes from 1.10.0-RC.
The only additional change is a fix for ProtoBuf packing of Kotlin unsigned types ([#​3079](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3079)).
Big thanks to [KosmX](https://redirect.github.com/KosmX) for contributing the fix.

> For your convenience, the changelog for 1.10.0-RC is duplicated below:

#### Stabilization of APIs

kotlinx-serialization 1.10 and subsequent releases will be focused on stabilization of existing APIs.
The following APIs and configuration options are no longer experimental because they're widely used without any known major issues:

- `Json` configuration options: `decodeEnumsCaseInsensitive`, `allowTrailingComma`, `allowComments`, and `prettyPrintIndent`. ([#​3100](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3100))
- `@EncodeDefault` annotation and its modes. ([#​3106](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3106))
- `JsonUnquotedLiteral` constructor function ([#​2900](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/2900))
- `JsonPrimitive` constructor function overloads that accept unsigned types. ([#​3117](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3117))
- JSON DSL functions on `JsonElement` with `Nothing?` overloads. ([#​3117](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3117))

#### Readiness for return value checker

Kotlin 2.3.0 [introduces a new feature](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/whatsnew23.html#unused-return-value-checker) aimed
at helping you to catch bugs related to the accidentally ignored return value of the function.
kotlinx-serialization 1.10.0-RC code is fully marked for this feature, meaning that you
can get warnings for unused function calls like `Json.encodeToString(...)`.
To get the warnings, the feature has to be enabled in your project as [described here](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/unused-return-value-checker.html#configure-the-unused-return-value-checker).

#### Polymorphism improvements

Polymorphic serialization received a couple of improvements in this release:

New `subclassesOfSealed` utility to automatically register sealed subclasses serializers in polymorphic modules ([#​2201](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/2201)).
Use it in your `SerializersModule` when configuring a polymorphic hierarchy which contains both abstract and sealed classes.
[For example](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/2199), when root of your hierarchy is an `interface`, but most of your inheritors are `sealed` classes.
The new function will register all known sealed subclasses for you, so you don’t need to list them one by one.
This makes writing your `SerializerModule`s much faster and simpler.
Big thanks to [Paul de Vrieze](https://redirect.github.com/pdvrieze) for contributing this feature.

Class discriminator conflict check rework ([#​3105](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3105)).
If a payload already contains a property with the same name as the configured discriminator (for example, `type`),
it is called a class discriminator conflict.
To produce a correct output and allow more inputs to be deserialized at the same time, the following changes were made:

- Conflicts introduced by `JsonNamingStrategy` transformations are now detected during serialization as well and will cause `SerializationException`.
  It also affects non-polymorphic classes.
- Conflicts from `ClassDisciminatorMode.ALL_JSON_OBJECTS` and `SerializersModuleBuilder.polymorphicDefaultSerializer` are also detected.
- It is allowed to deserialize such a conflicting key for both sealed and open polymorphic hierarchies.
  Previously, it was possible in the sealed hierarchies alone due to missing assertion. See [#​1664](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/1664) for details.

#### General improvements

- Add `.serialName` to `MissingFieldException` for clearer diagnostics. ([#​3114](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3114))
- Generate unique `Automatic-Module-Name` entries for metadata JARs. ([#​3109](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3109))
- Revised ProGuard rules and added R8 tests. ([#​3041](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3041))
- CBOR: Improved error message when a byte string/array type mismatch is encountered. ([#​3052](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3052))

#### Bugfixes

- Fix the type in the `BIGNUM_NEGATIVE` tag name. ([#​3090](https://redirect.github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx.serialization/issues/3090))

### Motivation
- Prevent Bluetooth/headset audio dropouts by initializing/resuming an `AudioContext` on user actions and keeping a near-silent oscillator running so SE/hint sounds don't lose their leading attack.

- Show the exact tone order (including inversion ordering) in the answer area so users can see the note sequence that was played.

- Bumped UI version to `ver1.2.3` and updated the changelog and visible version text in `GsRockCamp/games/qualities/index.html`.
- Removed the UI "D 開発中" box and adjusted layout spacing accordingly.
- Added `ensureAudioContext()`, `stopKeepAlive()`, a tiny `OscillatorNode` + `GainNode` keep-alive, and wired `resume()` logic to be invoked before playback via `playAudio`, `attemptPlay`, `playSnippet`, `playSfx`, and `playFixedSfx` so audio routes are kept awake; tied keep-alive to the SFX option and stop it when SFX is disabled via `loadSfxOption()`.

author: alex-nork
body:
The purpose of this PR is to rewrite the ambient analyzer system prompt so the agent suggests help for visible problems instead of passively documenting them as user "preferences."

## Problem

When the agent saw a Gmail inbox with 101K unread promotional emails, it created a knowledge base entry: "User maintains strict email segmentation... indicating deliberate inbox organization strategy." The correct reaction is to offer to help clean it up.

The root cause was a prompt that framed the agent as a passive observer — "learn about habits, preferences, and workflow" — with suggestions gated as rare exceptions. This caused the agent to rationalize problems as preferences rather than identifying them as opportunities to help.

## Changes Made

- Restructured the decision guide to clearly separate neutral observations (preferences, tools, workflow) from actionable problems (clutter, errors, debt)
- Added concrete examples of when to suggest: overflowing inboxes, digital debt, stale notifications, errors, repetitive work
- Added anti-rationalization rule: "Do NOT rationalize problems as 'preferences' or 'strategies'"
- Removed the "ignore ~80% of the time" quota that pushed the agent toward excessive passivity
- Added a litmus test: "Is this something the user would want fixed, cleaned up, or improved?"

## Testing

- Verified xcodebuild succeeds
- Manual validation against the original inbox screenshot scenario

author: michaelbonner
body:
## What

Moves the Zoho SalesIQ chat widget from `app.html` (render-blocking in `<head>`) to a dynamic script injection in `+layout.svelte` with a 3-second delay after mount.

## Why

The Zoho widget was loading on the main thread during initial page render, blocking critical resources. Since the chat widget isn't needed immediately on page load, deferring it improves:

- **Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)** - fewer scripts competing during initial render
- **Total Blocking Time (TBT)** - less main thread work during page load
- **Time to Interactive (TTI)** - page becomes interactive faster

## How

- Removed inline Zoho scripts from `app.html`
- Added dynamic script injection in `+layout.svelte` `onMount`, delayed by 3 seconds
- Added `Window.$zoho` type declaration to `app.d.ts`
- Chat functionality is fully preserved, it just loads after the page is interactive

author: hariombalhara
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds temporary debug logging to `no-show-updated-action.integration-test.ts` and `integration-utils.ts` to diagnose a flaky CI failure where the booking intermittently disappears between `beforeEach` and the test body assertion (`getAuditLogsForBooking` throws `BOOKING_NOT_FOUND_OR_PERMISSION_DENIED`).

This test passes locally every time but fails intermittently in CI across multiple unrelated PRs (#27546, #26792, #27664, #27772). The root cause is unknown — each test file creates unique data and no broad deletes exist. This PR instruments the test to capture exactly **when** the booking/user disappear relative to the test lifecycle.

**This is a temporary debugging PR — not intended for permanent merge.**

### Instrumentation added:

- **`no-show-updated-action.integration-test.ts`**: `checkBookingExists()` and `checkUserExists()` calls at every key point — end of `beforeEach`, start of each test, after `onBookingAction`, before `getAuditLogsForBooking`, and start of `afterEach`. When booking disappearance is detected, logs total booking/user counts and whether audit records still exist.
- **`integration-utils.ts`**: `cleanupLog()` at each step of `cleanupTestData` with PID and timestamp. Before user deletion, checks if the user still has associated bookings (to catch cascade delete evidence). This affects all 6 sibling booking-audit test files since they share this utility.

All logs include `process.pid` and ISO timestamps to correlate events across parallel test file processes.

## Mandatory Tasks (DO NOT REMOVE)

- [x] I have self-reviewed the code (A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected).
- N/A - No docs changes needed (temporary debugging instrumentation).
- N/A - No fix to test; this PR adds diagnostic logging only.

## How should this be tested?

1. CI integration tests will run automatically
2. If the flaky test fails, the CI logs will now contain `[DEBUG]` and `[CLEANUP]` lines showing the exact DB state at each point
3. Look for `!!! BOOKING DISAPPEARED !!!` in CI output to find the failure point
4. Cross-reference `[CLEANUP]` logs from other PIDs to see if a parallel file's cleanup overlapped

## Human Review Checklist

- [ ] **`integration-utils.ts` changes affect all 6 booking-audit test files** — the extra DB queries in `cleanupTestData` (checking user bookings before delete) add overhead to every test file that imports this utility. Acceptable for debugging but must be reverted.
- [ ] Verify this PR is kept in draft and not merged permanently — all logging should be removed once root cause is identified.

body:
The issue: The current system has a logic gap: when you mark as "Reminder", it queues a reminder email. But if you then mark as "Paid" before the reminder sends (or even after), the system doesn't properly handle the transition - it should send a confirmation instead, but only if the reminder was actually sent. Your proposed solution with "AD" (Amount Due) suffix for unpaid invoices is excellent. Let me implement this logic: Key Changes Needed:
Invoice Number Generation: Append "-AD" for Amount Due invoices Status Change Logic:
Direct "Paid": Check payment details → Generate normal invoice → Send confirmation "Reminder" → "Paid": Check if "Reminder Sent" exists → Generate new invoice (without -AD) → Send confirmation Email Queue Logic: Cancel pending reminders when status changes to Paid, but track if reminder was already sent

author: ringcanary
body:
⚡ Bolt: Optimized `elements_from_point` and `ElementsFromPoint`

💡 What:
Replaced `iter().flat_map().collect()` chains with `Vec::with_capacity(len)` and explicit loops pushing elements.

🎯 Why:
To reduce allocation churn in hit-testing hot paths. `collect()` from a `flat_map` cannot accurately predict the upper bound size, leading to potential reallocations. By manually retrieving the source vector and using its length as capacity, we ensure at most one allocation.

📊 Impact:
Reduces allocation overhead in `elements_from_point` calls, which are critical for user interaction responsiveness.

🔬 Measurement:
Verified by manual code inspection. `cargo test -p script` was run but failed due to unrelated environment issues (missing `llvm-objdump`), which is a known state for this environment. Logic was verified to be equivalent to the original implementation.

author: basic-bit
body:
[AGENT]

## What
- Capture Discord message attachments during meetings and persist them in meeting chat artifacts.
- Show attachment-only messages in the portal timeline (and exports) with clickable links.

## Why
- Today, image-only / attachment-only messages are dropped because we only store/render `message.content`.
- This makes meeting history incomplete and prevents users from finding referenced files later.

## Changes
- Add `ChatAttachment` + `ChatEntry.attachments` (`src/types/chat.ts`).
- Capture `message.attachments` in the meeting chat collector (`src/meetings.ts`).
- Persist attachments in `chat.json` (`src/services/uploadService.ts`) and include a compact attachment summary in `chat.txt` via `renderChatEntryLine` (`src/utils/chatLog.ts`).
- Emit timeline chat events even when content is empty if attachments exist, and carry attachments through the `MeetingEvent` type (`src/services/meetingTimelineService.ts`, `src/types/meetingTimeline.ts`).
- Render attachment links in the portal timeline (`src/frontend/components/MeetingTimeline.tsx`) and update story coverage (`src/frontend/components/MeetingTimeline.stories.tsx`).
- Improve auto-record cancellation samples to include attachment-only messages (`src/services/autoRecordCancellationService.ts`).

## Follow-ups
- #103 (image captions for shared images)
- #104 (agentic summarizer / chunking + retrieval)

## Testing
- `yarn check:ci`
- `yarn test-storybook`

Closes #20.

author: sujitbista
body:
**Summary**
Adds server-side validation for appointment status updates so invalid transitions are rejected with clear 400 errors (e.g. completing a PENDING appointment or confirming a past one).

**Changes**
New validator assertValidStatusTransition() in apps/api/src/services/appointment-status.validation.ts — single place for all transition rules, called from updateAppointment() before any DB write.
Wiring — updateAppointment() in appointment.service.ts calls the validator when status is in the update input; no change to DB schema or API response shape.
Unit tests — appointment-status.validation.test.ts (Vitest) for: PENDING→COMPLETED rejected, CONFIRMED→COMPLETED allowed when time OK / rejected when future, past CONFIRMED rejected, CANCELLED→CONFIRMED and COMPLETED→CANCELLED rejected, PENDING→CONFIRMED and PENDING/CONFIRMED→CANCELLED allowed, no-op and BOOKED/NO_SHOW cases.
Route test — “should reject COMPLETED when appointment is PENDING” in appointment.routes.test.ts (PUT with status: "COMPLETED" on PENDING → 400, message: “Cannot complete an unconfirmed appointment.”).

**Validation rules**
| Rule / Transition | Result |
|-------------------|--------|
| `CANCELLED` / `COMPLETED` / `NO_SHOW` → any | ❌ Reject (terminal statuses) |
| `PENDING` → `COMPLETED` | ❌ Reject — *Cannot complete an unconfirmed appointment* |
| Set to `CONFIRMED` when `now > appointmentEnd` | ❌ Reject — *Cannot confirm a past appointment* |
| `CONFIRMED` / `BOOKED` → `COMPLETED` when `now < appointmentStart` | ❌ Reject — *Cannot complete an appointment that hasn't started* |
| `PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` (when `now ≤ appointmentEnd`) | ✅ Allowed |
| `PENDING` / `CONFIRMED` / `BOOKED` → `CANCELLED` | ✅ Allowed |

**Error responses**
Same JSON shape as existing validation (e.g. confirm rejection): { success: false, error: { code, message, statusCode } }, status 400.
**Testing**
npm run test -- src/services/appointment-status.validation.test.ts — all 12 unit tests pass.
Appointment route tests may fail in CI if the test DB schema is out of date (e.g. missing cancelledBy / schedule_exceptions); those failures are environment/schema-related, not caused by this PR.
Checklist
[x] Backend only; no DB schema changes.
[x] Existing API response shape kept.
[x] Tests added for the validator and for PENDING→COMPLETED rejection.
[x] No breaking changes to existing successful update flows.

author: radaghastly
body:
## Summary

Closes #175. Adds a transparent HTTP + WebSocket reverse proxy that exposes agent gateways through AgentGate's public URL at `/px/<proxy-id>/`.

This lets mobile apps like ClawVoice connect to any agent's gateway through AgentGate without separate tunnels.

## Changes

### `src/routes/proxy.js` (new — 153 lines)
- `createProxyRouter()`: Express handler for HTTP reverse proxy
- `setupWebSocketProxy(server)`: Raw WebSocket upgrade handler for bidirectional piping
- Path stripping: `/px/<id>/hooks/wake` → `/hooks/wake`
- Error handling: 404 for disabled/unknown proxies, 502 for unreachable targets

### `src/lib/db.js`
- Migration: adds `gateway_proxy_enabled`, `gateway_proxy_id`, `gateway_proxy_url` columns to `api_keys`
- New functions: `getGatewayProxy()`, `updateGatewayProxy()`, `regenerateProxyId()`, `disableGatewayProxy()`, `listGatewayProxies()`
- Updated `listApiKeys()`, `getApiKeyById()`, `getApiKeyByName()` to include proxy fields

### `src/index.js`
- Proxy route mounted **before** body parsers (so request bodies pass through untouched)
- WebSocket upgrade handler set up after socket.io init

### `src/routes/ui/keys.js`
- New "Proxy" column on Agents table with status badge
- Configure modal: enable/disable, set gateway URL, copy proxy URL, regenerate proxy ID
- Endpoints: `POST /:id/proxy`, `POST /:id/regenerate-proxy`

### `tests/ui.test.js`
- Added mock functions for proxy DB operations

## Security
- Proxy **disabled by default** for all agents
- Unguessable proxy IDs (nanoid 32 chars)
- No new auth layer — target gateway handles its own authentication
- Admin can regenerate proxy ID to revoke access

## No new dependencies
Uses native Node.js `http`/`https` modules for both HTTP proxying and WebSocket upgrade piping.

body:
## Summary

Adds `userClaim` as an optional string field across all chat event types, extracted from `extras.userClaim` on realtime messages and from the REST response. This allows customers to use channel-specific JWT user claims with Chat.

The field is read-only and server-set via JWT claims — clients do not send it.

[CHA-1243]

## Changes

### Core SDK
- **Messages**: `userClaim` on `Message` type, extracted in `message-parser.ts` and `rest-types.ts`
- **Message Reactions**: `userClaim` on `MessageReactionRawEvent.reaction`
- **Typing**: `userClaim` on `TypingSetEvent.change`, tracked via merged `TypingClientState` map
- **Room Reactions**: `userClaim` on `RoomReaction` interface, extracted in `room-reaction-parser.ts`
- **Presence**: `userClaim` on `PresenceMember` type
- **RealtimeExtras**: Introduced `RealtimeExtras` type and `realtimeExtras()` helper in `realtime-extensions.ts` to replace unsafe `any` access on Ably `extras`

### Tests
- Integration tests for all five event types verifying `userClaim` propagation
- Unit tests for message parser and REST type conversion
- Assertions on both realtime subscriptions and REST API responses (`messages.get()`, `messages.history()`)

### Misc
- Removed stray `console.log` from `use-event-listener-ref.test.tsx`


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core event/types and parsing paths for realtime and REST, plus adjusts typing state semantics; changes are well-covered by added unit/integration tests but could impact downstream consumers relying on event shapes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds first-class support for *per-room JWT user claims* by exposing a read-only `userClaim?: string` across chat entities: `Message` (realtime + REST), `PresenceMember`, `RoomReaction`, and raw `MessageReactionRawEvent.reaction`, all parsed from `extras.userClaim` via a new typed `realtimeExtras()` helper.
> 
> Extends typing APIs to carry claim metadata by introducing `TypingSetEntry` and `Typing.currentTypers`/`TypingSetEvent.currentTypers` (while deprecating `currentlyTyping`), and updates the demo app to mint room-scoped claims and render stable display names derived from the claim. Tests are expanded with new unit/integration coverage validating claim propagation and the new typing shape, plus a small cleanup removing a stray `console.log`.
>

body:
Adds backend support for checkout.html PayPal integration. Existing `/pay/paypal` works with product IDs; new flow needs cart total-based order creation and explicit capture after approval.

## New Endpoints

- **POST `/api/paypal/create-order`** - Creates order from cart total
  ```json
  Request:  { "total": 29.99, "currency": "EUR", "cart": [...] }
  Response: { "orderID": "..." }
  ```

- **POST `/api/paypal/capture-order`** - Captures approved order
  ```json
  Request:  { "orderID": "..." }
  Response: { "id": "...", "status": "...", "payer": {...}, ... }
  ```

## Implementation

- **paypal_pay.py**: Extracted `create_paypal_order_from_amount()` and `capture_paypal_order()` helpers using `OrdersCreateRequest` and `OrdersCaptureRequest`. Legacy `create_paypal_order()` now delegates to shared logic.

- **main.py**: Added Pydantic models for type validation. Currency defaults to EUR (checkout.html standard). Errors return `{"error": "..."}` with 400/404 status codes. Logging added without exposing exception details.

- **README.md**: Documents required env vars (`PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID`, `PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET`) and API contract.

## Backward Compatibility

Legacy `/pay/paypal?product_id=N` endpoint unchanged (still uses USD).

author: naxty
body:
The `formae` binary was built to the repo root (`./formae`). The plugin loader in
`manager.go` resolves `../plugins` relative to the binary as its first search path.

If the parent directory happens to contain a `plugins/` folder (e.g. when the repo
lives at `pel/formae/` alongside `pel/plugins/` for external plugins), the loader
picks up the wrong directory and never finds the internal `.so` plugins like `pkl.so`.

This moves the binary output to `bin/formae` so that `../plugins` correctly resolves
to `./plugins/` where the built `.so` files live.

Symptom: `formae agent start` shows `ERR no plugin found for file extension: .pkl`
with no other error or warning.

author: julianken
body:
## Summary

- Add new `mobile-app` package with app lifecycle management for React Native
- Implement `useAppLifecycle` hook that subscribes to AppState and coordinates database suspend/resume
- Create `DatabaseProvider` React context that integrates lifecycle handling with database initialization
- Add 30 comprehensive unit tests covering all lifecycle scenarios

## Changes

### New Package: `@double-bind/mobile-app`

**Hooks:**
- `useAppLifecycle(db, options)` - Manages app lifecycle events for database operations
  - Calls `db.suspend()` when app goes to background (flushes pending writes)
  - Calls `db.resume()` when app returns to foreground (validates state)
  - Debounces rapid transitions to prevent state corruption
  - Handles iOS inactive state transitions
- `useAppLifecycleState()` - Observe app state without database integration

**Providers:**
- `DatabaseProvider` - React context provider for database access
  - Initializes `MobileGraphDB` on mount
  - Integrates lifecycle handling automatically
  - Cleans up database on unmount
- `useDatabase()` - Access database context (db, isReady, error, isSuspended)
- `useDatabaseInstance()` - Direct database access (throws if not ready)

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests for `useAppLifecycle` hook (19 tests)
  - [x] Subscribe/unsubscribe to AppState
  - [x] Background transition calls `db.suspend()`
  - [x] Foreground transition calls `db.resume()`
  - [x] Error handling for suspend/resume failures
  - [x] Debouncing rapid state changes
  - [x] iOS inactive state handling
  - [x] State deduplication
- [x] Unit tests for `DatabaseProvider` (11 tests)
  - [x] Database initialization with path
  - [x] onReady/onError callbacks
  - [x] Database cleanup on unmount
  - [x] Context value provides correct state
  - [x] Hook throws outside provider

## Acceptance Criteria (DBB-380)

- [x] Database suspends on background
- [x] Database resumes on foreground
- [x] State persisted correctly across app restarts

## Summary
Added period navigation functionality to the RootHomeTabPeriodSubCategory screen, allowing users to navigate between months and adjust the date range being displayed.

## Key Changes
- **UI Layout Restructuring**: Moved the period selector (month navigation and range buttons) from the LoadedContent to the main screen content, making it visible regardless of loading state
- **Period Navigation Methods**: Implemented three new navigation methods in the ViewModel:
  - `onClickNextMonth()` - advances the display period by one month
  - `onClickPreviousMonth()` - moves back one month
  - `onClickRange(range: Int)` - adjusts the viewing window to a specific number of months
- **State Synchronization**: Added `updateStructure()` method to sync the ViewModel state with navigation parameters when the screen is accessed
- **UI State Enhancement**: 
  - Added `PeriodUiState` data class to hold period display information (between dates and range text)
  - Updated `RootHomeTabPeriodSubCategoryContentUiState` to include period UI state
  - Added corresponding event handlers to the Event interface
- **Navigation Integration**: Period changes now trigger navigation updates via `emitNavigationUpdate()`, ensuring the navigation stack reflects the current viewing period

## Implementation Details
- Period navigation updates are persisted through the navigation structure, allowing the view to maintain state across navigation
- The period selector UI is now consistently displayed at the top of the screen using `RootHomePeriodSection` component
- The display period is calculated and formatted in a companion object helper function for consistency

author: gkdl0471-code
body:
<!-- PR 제목 규칙:
[type]: 작업 요약 (#이슈번호)
예시: feat: 로그인 페이지 UI 구현 (#12)
-->

## #️⃣ 연관된 이슈

- Resolves #160 

## 📑 구현 사항

- **Ordering(순서 맞추기) 문항**
  - API 문항 타입 상수 매핑 (`EXAM_QUESTION_TYPE_TO_API`, `API_TO_EXAM_QUESTION_TYPE`) 추가 후 문항 타입을 API 스펙에 맞춰 렌더링
  - Ordering 컴포넌트: 슬롯 간 **맞바꾸기(swap)**, 슬롯 내 **라벨 드래그**로 순서 변경, 중간 슬롯 제거 시 **자리 유지**
  - 결과 조회 응답 타입·매퍼 보강(snake_case, null 처리) 및 결과 페이지에서 Ordering 정답/해설 표시

- **응시 페이지 이탈 경고**
  - **브라우저 뒤로가기**: `popstate` 리스너 + 동일 URL로 `history.pushState` 한 번 추가 → 뒤로가기 시 같은 퀴즈 URL로만 이동해 라우트 유지 후 이탈 경고 모달 표시
  - **헤더 뒤로가기 링크**: `QuizHeader`에 `onBackClick` prop 추가 → 클릭 시 바로 이탈 경고 모달만 표시(다른 페이지로 이동하지 않음)
  - 모달 **확인** 시 `submitAndNavigateFromLeave()`로 답안 자동 제출 후 결과 페이지 이동, **닫기** 시 모달만 닫고 응시 페이지 유지

- **부정행위·전체화면**
  - 부정행위 경고 모달 확인 시 전체화면이 아니면 전체화면으로 전환 후 모달 닫기
  - 결과 페이지 / 마이페이지 퀴즈 목록 진입 시 전체화면이면 자동 해제

- **기타**
  - 결과 페이지 응시시간 0분 표시 개선(elapsed_time 우선, 음수 방지)

---

## 🌀 어려웠던 점 / 고민했던 부분

- **브라우저 뒤로가기 시 모달이 안 뜨는 문제**
  - `useBlocker`는 데이터 라우터(createBrowserRouter)에서만 동작하고, 현재 앱은 `BrowserRouter`를 사용해 에러로 인해 빈 화면이 나옴 → `useBlocker` 제거 후 **History API(popstate + pushState)** 로 처리
  - 뒤로가기 한 번에 이전 페이지로 나가면 React Router가 라우트를 바꿔 QuizPage가 언마운트되어 모달을 띄울 수 없음 → **진입 시 동일 URL로 `pushState` 한 번** 해서 히스토리를 `[이전, 퀴즈, 퀴즈]`처럼 만들고, 뒤로가기를 누르면 같은 퀴즈 URL로만 이동하도록 해 라우트 유지 후 모달 표시

- **헤더 뒤로가기 링크**
  - `<Link to="/mypage/quiz">`는 클릭 시 바로 이동하므로 `popstate`가 발생하지 않음 → 헤더에 **`onBackClick` 옵션**을 두고, 응시 페이지에서는 링크 대신 버튼으로 렌더링해 클릭 시 `setOpenModal('leaveWarning')`만 호출하도록 분기

- **popstate 핸들러에서 setState**
  - popstate 콜백이 예전 클로저의 `setOpenModal`을 참조할 수 있어, **ref에 최신 `setOpenModal`을 넣어 두고** `setOpenModalRef.current('leaveWarning')`로 호출하도록 변경

- **Ordering 슬롯·드래그**
  - 라벨을 슬롯에 넣었다 뺐다 할 때 인덱스 꼬임과 자리 유지 요구사항을 맞추기 위해, 슬롯 배열 초기화·드래그 종료 시 swap/제거 로직을 정리하고 `@dnd-kit`의 `useDraggable`/`useDroppable`로 라벨·슬롯 드래그를 일관되게 처리

---

## 📸 구현 이미지

---
- **Ordering 디벨롭**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a493fa9-2894-4001-8231-69602acf6c1d

- **응시 중 뒤로가기 패치 ver.1**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c998eab9-2be6-445a-9c6d-3eb764e38bc3

- **응시 중 뒤로가기 패치 ver.2**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdfe20a8-7a73-4ba1-9062-67fa5a050ce7



## ❇️ 코드 설명

- **이탈 경고**: QuizPage에서 `popstate` 리스너 + 진입 시 동일 URL `pushState`로 뒤로가기 시 모달 표시·URL 유지. 확인 시 `handleLeaveWarningConfirm` → `submitAndNavigateFromLeave()`로 제출 후 결과 페이지 이동.
- **QuizHeader**: `onBackClick` 전달 시 Link 대신 button 렌더링, 클릭 시 이탈 경고 모달만 오픈.
- **useQuizSubmissionFlow**: `submitAndNavigateFromLeave`에서 payload 제출 후 성공 시 결과 페이지, 실패 시 목록으로 이동.
- **Ordering**: `@dnd-kit`으로 라벨↔슬롯 드래그·슬롯 간 swap·제거 시 해당 슬롯만 비우며 자리 유지.
- **전체화면**: QuizResultPage·MyPageQuiz 마운트 시 `fullscreenElement` 있으면 `exitFullscreen()` 호출.

## 💬 리뷰 요청사항

> 리뷰어에게 피드백을 받고 싶은 지점이 있다면 작성해주세요.

author: bruffstar
body:
## Summary

This branch fixes critical chat bugs, adds real-time session context tracking with compaction awareness, builds a comprehensive test suite, and sets up a full CI pipeline with security checks.

## Changes

### Bug fixes
- **FTS5 desync fix** — `deleteChannel()` was dropping the FTS delete trigger before deleting messages, leaving orphaned FTS entries. New messages reusing those rowids caused `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_PRIMARYKEY` crashes. Now keeps the trigger active and falls back to rebuild on failure.
- **FTS auto-repair** — `createMessage`, `updateMessage`, `deleteMessage`, and `searchMessages` all catch FTS constraint/sync errors and automatically rebuild the index then retry.
- **Typing indicator pixel shift** — Replaced standalone `TypingIndicator` component with `MessageBubble` reuse via `isTypingIndicator` prop. Same component = zero layout shift.

### Session context & compaction tracking
- **New `/api/openclaw/session/status` route** — Reads session data directly from the OpenClaw filesystem store instead of going through Gateway RPC. Resolves effective context limits from OpenClaw config (per-agent override → global default → 200k hardcoded default). Includes full system prompt breakdown (project context, skills, tools, workspace files).
- **New `/api/openclaw/session/context` route** — Determines the compaction boundary: which messages the agent can still "see". Calls `sessions.preview` on the Gateway, matches against local DB timestamps, caches result.
- **New `useCompactionEvents` hook** — Subscribes to real-time compaction events via SSE singleton. Tracks compaction start/end, shows auto-dismissing banner, fires callback to refresh session stats.
- **New `useContextBoundary` hook** — Fetches and caches the compaction boundary message ID. Messages before this boundary are visually dimmed in the UI.
- **New `SSE singleton`** — Single shared `EventSource` connection ref-counted across all hooks. Deduplicates events by sequence number, pattern-based subscription (`"chat"`, `"agent.*"`, `"*"`).
- **Redesigned `SessionStatsPanel`** — Compact inline indicator with SVG border progress ring showing context usage. Expands to full modal with token breakdown, thinking level, compaction count, and system prompt details (skills, tools, workspace files with truncation warnings).
- **Schema change** — Added `compaction_boundary_message_id` column to sessions table.
- **Updated `SessionStatus` type** — Now includes `modelProvider`, `total` tokens, `modelMax` context, `thinkingLevel`, and full `systemPrompt` breakdown.

### UI improvements
- Message navigation with Shift+Up/Down
- Scroll-to-message-start button for long agent responses
- Channel loading skeletons
- Custom dot-bounce animation for typing indicator

### Dev logging
- Structured logging across Gateway RPC (method/duration/errors), SSE lifecycle, all API routes (entry/exit with timing), DB operations (error context), and client hooks (send/receive/orphan/timeout failures).

### Test suite
- **201+ unit tests across 20 files** — DB queries, API routes (chat, channels, search, settings, ping, agents, config, session status), hooks (use-chat, use-openclaw, use-search, use-session-stats, use-agent-status), config, gateway connection, SSE singleton, api-security, date-utils, utils.
- **3 integration test suites** — Chat lifecycle (multi-route flow with real DB), Gateway WebSocket (real `ws` server), failure recovery (optimistic cleanup, retry, idempotency).
- All tests use isolated in-memory SQLite via `installTestDb()` — no live services touched.

### CI pipeline & open source
- **GitHub Actions CI** on PRs to main: secret scanning (generic + OpenClaw-specific `rew_` tokens, device keys, remote WebSocket URLs), sensitive file detection (`.env`, `.pem`, `.key`, DB files, backups, logs, `.npmrc`), large file check (>512KB), `console.log` detection in source, `npm audit`, version bump enforcement, lint, test, build.
- **Auto-tagging** — On merge to main, reads version from `package.json` and creates `vX.Y.Z` git tag.
- **npm publish safety** — `files` field in `package.json` scopes published package to only runtime files (excludes tests, CI, community files).
- **Branch protection** — CI + 1 review required, linear history, no force push, stale reviews dismissed.
- `LICENSE` (MIT), `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, issue templates, PR template.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test` passes (201+ tests)
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes
- [ ] `npm run build` passes
- [ ] `npm pack --dry-run` confirms no test/CI files in package
- [ ] Version bumped in `package.json`

author: xrfxlp
body:
## Summary

This PR adds gang discovery as a prerequisite for multi-node NCCL tests (follow-up PR).
### Overview
Gang discovery identifies pods belonging to the same scheduling group. Pods contain a "gang anchor" (reference to a parent object) which holds gang metadata like minMember (minimum ready pods required).
Two discovery mechanisms:
1. Native Kubernetes (1.35+): Pod's spec.schedulingGates references a Workload object containing minMember
2. PodGroup-based schedulers (Volcano, etc.): Pod annotation/label points to a PodGroup CRD. Config-driven: specify annotation key, GVR for the PodGroup resource and CEL path for minCount for podgroup completion.

Coordination via ConfigMap:
1. Webhook creates a skeleton ConfigMap at admission time
2. Gang controller populates it with peer IPs as pods become ready
3. Init containers read ConfigMap to discover master address and peer list

**Key assumption**: Gang membership must be determinable at admission time (before pod is scheduled) to inject preflight init containers.


## Testing
### Kubernetes native using [workload API](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/workload-api/)
Gang discovery in configmap:
```
$ kg cm preflight-config -n nvsentinel -o yaml | yq '.data["config.yaml"]' | yq .gangDiscovery
{}
```

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a public submission workflow so external URLs can be queued, smoke-tested, and linked back into QA storage for inspection in the dashboard.
- Ensure submissions are persisted, processed sequentially, and surfaced via the existing QA UI and APIs.

### Description
- Add a persistent submission queue implementation in `src/ui/submissions.ts` that stores records in `qa-storage/submissions.json`, runs a small smoke `TestCase` suite via `runTestSuite`, and links created test-run records using a `submission:<id>` tag.
- Extend `src/ui/server.ts` to initialize the `SubmissionQueue`, add endpoints for `GET /api/submissions`, `POST /api/submissions`, and `POST /api/submissions/:id/retry`, and add helpers `parseJsonBody` and `isValidHttpUrl` for safe request handling.
- Update the dashboard UI by modifying `src/ui/public/index.html`, `src/ui/public/app.js`, and `src/ui/public/styles.css` to add a submission form, submission list and detail views, client-side create/retry actions, and new status badges/styles.
- Implement a small smoke test recipe `buildSubmissionTestCases` that navigates, observes, and extracts summary content for submitted URLs to detect gross failures.

### Testing
- Attempted to start the UI server using `pnpm tsx src/ui/server.ts` and `pnpm dlx tsx src/ui/server.ts`, but both attempts failed due to missing `tsx` / npm registry access errors (no running server was produced).
- No automated test suite or unit tests were executed against the changes in CI or locally due to the environment/tooling limitations. 
- Static validation performed: file changes were added and format/exports aligned with existing modules, but runtime validation was not completed because the server could not be launched.

author: ringxworld
body:
## Summary

Adds deterministic PNG graph export support for the dashboard while keeping existing SVG export behavior unchanged. This gives API and CLI users a reproducible raster export path for docs/reporting workflows.

## Linked Issues

- https://github.com/ringxworld/story_generator/issues/96
- https://github.com/ringxworld/story_generator/issues/9

## Merge Gates

Before requesting merge, expect these required checks to pass on `develop`/`main`:

- `label`
- `pr-template`
- `quality`
- `frontend`
- `pages`
- `native`
- `docker`

Local command that mirrors the full gate:

- `make check`

## Full Mode (Larger/Riskier Change)

### Motivation / Context

The dashboard export surface only exposed SVG payloads. Consumers that need deterministic PNG artifacts had no built-in path and had to convert externally. This change introduces a first-party deterministic PNG export path without adding heavy runtime dependencies.

### What Changed

- Added:
  - deterministic PNG renderer in `src/story_gen/core/dashboard_views.py`
  - new API response contract `DashboardGraphPngExportResponse`
  - new endpoint `GET /api/v1/stories/{story_id}/dashboard/graph/export.png`
  - new CLI entrypoint `story-dashboard-export` (`--format svg|png`)
  - ADR `docs/adr/0021-dashboard-png-export-surface.md`
- Changed:
  - contract registry entries and exported registry artifact
  - API docs and graph strategy docs
  - MkDocs nav and ADR index
  - tests for API/core/CLI/project contracts
- Removed:
  - none

### Tradeoffs and Risks

- Performance impacts:
  - PNG rendering is CPU-bound pure Python; acceptable for current graph sizes.
- Behavior changes:
  - API root now lists a new PNG export endpoint.
- Edge cases that still exist:
  - this slice targets graph export only; timeline/theme PNG export remains follow-up work for full #96 scope.
- Things deliberately left out:
  - no new external image dependencies.

### How This Was Tested

- Unit tests added or updated:
  - `tests/test_story_analysis_pipeline.py`
  - `tests/test_api_app.py`
  - `tests/test_cli_entrypoints.py`
  - `tests/test_project_contracts.py`
  - `tests/test_contract_registry.py`
- Manual test cases run:
  - full repository checks.
- Inputs used to validate behavior:
  - fixed story inputs and repeated PNG export comparisons for deterministic output.
- Not tested (if any):
  - large-scale export performance benchmarking.

### Follow-ups / Future Work (Optional)

- Extend deterministic PNG/SVG export coverage beyond graph to timeline/theme surfaces for complete #96 acceptance.

body:
### Motivation
- Move the signing flow to email-only and remove/soft-deprecate phone/telegram flows while making sign sessions robust and test-friendly. 
- Ensure DB has needed indexes and columns for fast lookup and compatibility with the new email session flow. 
- Prevent test hangs by making repo calls context-aware and adding timeouts around long-running operations.

### Description
- Postman: refreshed signing collection to an email-only flow and cleaned environment variables; updated file `postman/KUB.postman_collection.json` and `postman/KUB.postman_environment.json` to include requests: `Start Signing (Email)`, `Signing Status`, `Verify Email Token (GET)`, `Confirm Email Token (POST)`, `Serve Sign Page (GET)`, `Sign Session (POST)` and removed/hid Telegram/phone requests and unused variables.
- Migrations: added `db/migrations/005_signing_indexes.up.sql` to create indexes on `signature_confirmations(token_hash)`, `(document_id,status)`, `expires_at` and similarly for `sign_sessions`; added `db/migrations/006_signature_confirmations_created_at.up.sql` to ensure `created_at` exists on `signature_confirmations`.
- Repositories / DB calls: made `SignSessionRepository` context-aware (`Create`, `GetByTokenHash`, `GetByID`, `FindSignedByDocumentEmail`, `CountRecentByDocumentID`, `CountRecentByPhone`, `Update`, `IncrementAttempts`) and switched to `QueryRowContext` / `ExecContext` / `QueryRowContext` usage to allow cancellation/timeouts.
- Services / Timeouts: added `withTimeout` helper and wrapped public sign-confirm and sign-session service methods with `context.WithTimeout(5s)`; updated `SignSessionService` to support `CreateEmailSession`, `ValidateSessionForPage`, and `SignByID` for email token → session → page → sign flow, and added validations/errors for edge cases.
- Handlers / Routes: updated `DocumentSigningConfirmationHandler` to create email-based sign sessions on confirm and return `session_id`, `sign_url`, `expires_at`; added sign-session endpoints under `/api/v1/sign/sessions/:id/page` (GET) and `/api/v1/sign/sessions/:id/sign` (POST); adjusted handlers to log and handle errors more clearly; removed Telegram/phone routes from Postman and replaced deprecated phone endpoints with deprecation responses in handlers.
- Models / Tests: added `SignerEmail` and `DocHash` to `SignSession` model; added/updated unit tests including `internal/services/email_sign_session_flow_test.go` (end-to-end email sign session flow), and updated existing tests to use context-aware repo signatures and to avoid hanging by using background contexts plus timeouts where appropriate.
- Config/tests: made `internal/config/config_test.go` resilient by writing a temporary config for tests and setting `SignConfirmPolicy` default so config tests run without external files.

### Testing
- Ran the full test suite with `go test ./... -count=1 -timeout 60s` and fixed failures iteratively until green; final run completed successfully with packages reporting `ok` for relevant units.
- Notable automated test results: `internal/config` and `internal/services` packages pass; end-to-end unit tests for the email sign session flow run under `internal/services` and succeed.
- The changes include adding timeouts/context to repository and service calls to eliminate previous test hangs; `QueryRowContext`/`ExecContext` usage was validated via the test run above.

body:
Implements AC grid TIF file management with automatic geographic coordinate extraction via GDAL.

## Backend (`apps/ac_data/`)
- **Model**: `AcTif` with DECIMAL(11,7) coordinate fields, indexed for spatial queries
- **Views**: CRUD endpoints with file upload, coordinate extraction, search/pagination
- **GDAL Integration**: Extracts bounding box from GeoTransform; gracefully degrades if unavailable
- **File Management**: Auto-naming `{id}_{lon}_{lat}.tif`, atomic move with `shutil.move`, cleanup on delete

## Frontend (`templates/ac_data/ac_list.html`)
- LayUI table with 6-field search (name, coordinates), file upload component (.tif only, 200MB limit)
- Inline edit via `layer.prompt`, delete confirmation

## Configuration
- **settings.py**: 200MB upload limits, conditional `ALLOWED_HOSTS`
- **urls.py**: 5 routes (`/ac/data/{list,upload,edit,delete}`)
- **sql/init.sql**: `ac_tif` schema with coordinate indexes

## Database Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE ac_tif (
  id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
  local_path varchar(200),
  ac_name varchar(200),
  ac_local_name varchar(200),
  start_longitude DECIMAL(11,7),
  end_longitude DECIMAL(11,7),
  start_latitude DECIMAL(11,7),
  end_latitude DECIMAL(11,7),
  KEY idx_ac_name (ac_name),
  KEY idx_longitude (start_longitude, end_longitude, start_latitude, end_latitude)
);
```

Compatible with SQLite (test) and MySQL (production) via `USE_MYSQL` environment variable.

## 需求概述

在现有仓库管理系统中新增 **AC栅格数据管理模块**，包含完整的前端页面和后端Python代码，支持AC栅格TIF文件的上传、列表展示、搜索、编辑、删除功能。

## 现有项目结构

项目使用 Django 4.2 + layui 前端框架，已有的 `system` 应用位于 `apps/system/` 目录下。项目支持 SQLite（测试）和 MySQL（生产）两种数据库，通过环境变量 `USE_MYSQL` 切换。

现有目录结构：
```
warehouse_manage_web2/
├── apps/
│   └── system/           # 已有的系统管理模块
├── manage.py
├── requirements.txt      # 当前：Django==4.2.26, Pillow==10.3.0, mysqlclient==2.2.0
├── sql/
│   └── init.sql
├── static/
│   └── layui/
├── templates/
│   ├── login.html
│   └── index.html
├── warehouse_manage/
│   ├── settings.py
│   ├── urls.py
│   ├── wsgi.py
│   └── asgi.py
├── README.md
└── DEPLOYMENT.md
```

关键配置参考（`warehouse_manage/settings.py`）：
- `sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(BASE_DIR, 'apps'))` — 应用位于 `apps/` 下
- `INSTALLED_APPS` 中注册应用时直接用模块名，如 `'system'`
- 模板目录：`os.path.join(BASE_DIR, 'templates')`
- 静态文件：`/static/layui/layui/css/layui.css`
- 数据库切换：`USE_MYSQL = os.environ.get('USE_MYSQL', 'False') == 'True'`
- `X_FRAME_OPTIONS = 'SAMEORIGIN'`（页面通过 iframe 嵌入）
- 登录中间件豁免 URL 列表在 `apps/system/middleware.py`

URL 路由在 `warehouse_manage/urls.py` 中，当前 import 方式：`from system import views`。

## 功能需求详细说明

### 1. 数据库表结构（MySQL）

```sql
-- ac栅格数据表
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `ac_tif` (
  `id` bigint NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `local_path` varchar(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT '' COMMENT 'ac数据服务器地址',
  `ac_name` varchar(200) NOT NULL COMMENT 'ac文件名称：上传时文件名称',
  `ac_local_name` varchar(200) NOT NULL COMMENT 'ac文件本地名称：id_起始经度_结束经度_起始纬度_结束纬度',
  `start_longitude` DECIMAL(11, 7) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '起始经度',
  `end_longitude` DECIMAL(11, 7) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '结束经度',
  `start_latitude` DECIMAL(11, 7) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '起始纬度',
  `end_latitude` DECIMAL(11, 7) DEFAULT NULL COMMENT '结束纬度',
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP COMMENT '创建时间',
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP COMMENT '更新时间',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `idx_ac_name` (`ac_name`),
  KEY `idx_longitude` (`start_longitude`,`end_longitude`,`start_latitude`,`end_latitude`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci COMMENT='ac栅格数据表';
```

### 2. 前端页面 `ac_list.html`

- **技术栈**：使用 layui 框架（引用 `/static/layui/layui/css/layui.css` 和 `/static/layui/layui/layui.js`）
- **列表展示字段**：id、文件名称(ac_name)、文件本地名称(ac_local_name)、起始经度(start_longitude)、结束经度(end_longitude)、起始纬度(start_latitude)、结束纬度(end_latitude)
- **搜索功能**：支持根据文件名称、文件本地名称、起始经度、结束经度、起始纬度、结束纬度进行检索
- **上传功能**：
  - 界面显示上传文件框和上传按钮
  - 只允许上传扩展名为 `.tif` 的文件
  - 文件大小不超过 200MB
  - 上传后刷新列表
- **编辑功能**：只可以编辑文件名称(ac_name)，编辑后刷新列表
- **删除功能**：删除时提示确认，同时删除服务器上的文件，删除后刷新列表
- **分页功能**：支持分页显示

### 3. 后端 API 接口

在 `apps/` 下创建新的 Django 应用 `ac_data`，包含以下文件：

#### 3.1 Model (`apps/ac_data/models.py`)
- 创建 `AcTif` 模型，映射到 `ac_tif` 表
- 字段与上述 SQL 表结构对应

#### 3.2 Views (`apps/ac_data/views.py`)
- **页面视图** `ac_list_page_view`：渲染 ac_list.html 页面
- **列表接口** `ac_list_view`：GET，支持分页和搜索，返回 JSON 格式 `{"code": 0, "msg": "成功", "count": total, "data": [...]}`
- **上传接口** `ac_upload_view`：POST，接收 .tif 文件
  - 使用 GDAL（`osgeo` 库）从上传的 TIF 文件中提取经纬度范围（GeoTransform）
  - 先保存数据库记录获得 id，然后按命名规则 `{id}_{start_longitude}_{end_longitude}_{start_latitude}_{end_latitude}.tif` 命名
  - 文件保存到项目根目录 `data/ac/` 下
  - `local_path` 保存为 `data/ac/{ac_local_name}.tif`
- **编辑接口** `ac_edit_view`：POST，只允许修改 `ac_name` 字段
- **删除接口** `ac_delete_view`：POST，删除数据库记录同时删除服务器上的文件

#### 3.3 Apps Config (`apps/ac_data/apps.py`)
```python
class AcDataConfig(AppConfig):
    default_auto_field = 'django.db.models.BigAutoField'
    name = 'ac_data'
```

### 4. URL 路由配置

在 `warehouse_manage/urls.py` 中新增路由：
```python
from ac_data import views as ac_views

# AC栅格数据管理
path('ac/data/list/', ac_views.ac_list_page_view, name='ac_list_page'),
path('ac/data/list/data/', ac_views.ac_list_view, name='ac_list'),
path('ac/data/upload/', ac_views.ac_upload_view, name='ac_upload'),
path('ac/data/edit/', ac_views.ac_edit_view, name='ac_edit'),
path('ac/data/delete/', ac_views.ac_delete_view, name='ac_delete'),
```

### 5. 注册应用

在 `warehouse_manage/settings.py` 的 `INSTALLED_APPS` 中添加 `'ac_data'`。

### 6. 文件上传配置

在 `settings.py` 中确保配置：
- `DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` 设置为 200MB 以上（如 `209715200`）
- `FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` 也适当调大
- 确保 `data/ac/` 目录存在（代码中自动创建）

### 7. requirements.txt 更新

在 `requirements.txt` 中添加 `GDAL` 依赖。注意：GDAL Python 绑定需要系统先安装 GDAL 库。

### 8. SQL 文件更新

在 `sql/init.sql` 末尾追加 `ac_tif` 表的建表语句和测试数据插入语句。

### 9. Django Migration

为 `ac_data` 应用创建初始 migration 文件 `apps/ac_data/migrations/0001_initial.py`。

### 10. README.md 更新

更新 README.md 增加：
- AC栅格数据管理模块的技术架构说明
- GDAL 安装说明（Ubuntu/CentOS/macOS）
- 数据库切换说明（SQLite vs MySQL）
- AC模块 API 接口文档
- 技术栈说明（Django, layui, GDAL, SQLite/MySQL 各自在系统中的使用位置）

## 代码质量要求

1. **命名规范**：包名、接口路径、类名、变量名、数据库字段等必须使用英文
2. **注释规范**：Python 方法需要有方法注释和参数注释，注释必须使用中文；其他主要功能也需要有中文注释
3. **数据库切换**：测试环境使用 SQLite，线上使用 MySQL，两数据库可自由切换
4. **企业级代码**：可扩展的架构，清晰的分层，完善的错误处理
5. **安全性**：文件类型验证、文件大小限制、SQL 注入防护（使用 ORM）、CSRF 保护（上传接口使用 `@csrf_exempt` 但需在前端传递 CSRF token）
6. **所有功能必须可用无 bug，...

body:
## Summary

Define the `CheckedArithmetic` trait providing fallible arithmetic operations (`safe_add`, `safe_sub`, `safe_mul`, `safe_div`, `safe_add_u128`) that return `Result<Self, AmmError>` with specific error variants. Implement for `Amount` and `Liquidity`. Price implementation is deferred until PR #49 (Issue #9) merges.

## Changes

- **src/math/checked.rs**: `CheckedArithmetic` trait definition + implementations
  - Trait methods: `safe_add`, `safe_sub`, `safe_mul`, `safe_div(rounding)`, `safe_add_u128`
  - All return `Result<Self, AmmError>` with specific variants:
    - `safe_add` / `safe_mul` / `safe_add_u128` → `AmmError::Overflow`
    - `safe_sub` → `AmmError::Underflow`
    - `safe_div` → `AmmError::DivisionByZero`
  - `Amount` impl: delegates to existing `checked_*` inherent methods
  - `Liquidity` impl: delegates to `checked_add`/`checked_sub`, inline `u128` ops for `safe_mul`/`safe_div`
  - Liquidity `safe_div` implements ceiling division for `Rounding::Up`
  - All impl methods marked `#[inline]`

- **src/math/mod.rs**: Added `checked` submodule and `CheckedArithmetic` re-export
- **src/prelude.rs**: Uncommented `CheckedArithmetic` re-export

## Technical Decisions

- **`safe_*` naming (not `checked_*`)**: Avoids conflict with existing inherent `checked_*` methods on `Amount` and `Liquidity` that return `Option`. The `safe_*` methods return `Result<Self, AmmError>` with specific error variants, enabling `?` propagation and error discrimination.
- **Price impl deferred**: `Price` is not on `main` yet (PR #49, Issue #9). Will be added in a follow-up once merged.
- **Liquidity inline division**: `Liquidity` lacks an inherent `checked_div` method. The `safe_div` implementation uses inline `u128` division with the same ceiling-division formula as `Amount::checked_div`.
- **Result-returning methods support chaining**: `a.safe_add(&b)?.safe_mul(&c)?` pattern works naturally with `?` operator.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added (26 new tests across 2 submodules)
  - Amount: 13 tests (safe_add/sub/mul/div success + error, safe_add_u128, chaining)
  - Liquidity: 13 tests (same coverage)
  - Tests verify correct `AmmError` variant for each error case
- [x] Doc-test added (1 new)
- [x] Manual testing performed (`cargo test --all-features` — 179 passed, 12 doc-tests passed)

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows `.internalDoc/09-RUST-GUIDELINES.md`
- [x] All public items have `///` documentation
- [x] No warnings from `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check` passes
- [x] Feature-gated code compiles with and without its feature
- [x] No `.unwrap()`, `.expect()`, or panics in library code

author: tuttimann
body:
## Summary

Adds the `--ir` (include resident data) flag to the `MFTECmd_$MFT.mkape` module, enabling resident data extraction in CSV/JSON output by default.

## Background

[MFTECmd PR #45](https://github.com/EricZimmerman/MFTECmd/pull/45) introduces the `--ir` flag which includes `ResidentDataBase64`, `ResidentDataHex`, and `ResidentDataASCII` fields in the output. This is highly valuable for forensic analysis — especially for small files stored entirely within MFT records (typically up to ~700-900 bytes).

## Changes

Updated both CSV and JSON `CommandLine` entries in `MFTECmd_$MFT.mkape` to include `--ir`:

```diff
- CommandLine: -f %sourceFile% --csv %destinationDirectory%
+ CommandLine: -f %sourceFile% --csv %destinationDirectory% --ir
- CommandLine: -f %sourceFile% --json %destinationDirectory%
+ CommandLine: -f %sourceFile% --json %destinationDirectory% --ir
```

## Rationale

Resident data extraction is a common DFIR use case (recovering small scripts, config files, or artifacts stored inline in the MFT). Having this enabled by default saves analysts a manual step during triage collections. Performance impact is minimal with the default 1024-byte size limit.

## Related

- MFTECmd PR: https://github.com/EricZimmerman/MFTECmd/pull/45

author: saharbarak
body:
## Summary

Implements automated performance regression detection via Lighthouse CI, uptime monitoring, and client-side error tracking.

### Changes

**Lighthouse CI** (`.github/workflows/lighthouse-ci.yml`)
- Runs on every PR touching `frontend/` files
- 3 Lighthouse runs per audit (desktop preset)
- Posts performance scores & Core Web Vitals as PR comment
- Uploads reports as artifacts (30-day retention)

**Performance Budgets** (`frontend/lighthouserc.js`)
- Performance >= 90, Accessibility >= 95, Best Practices >= 90
- LCP <= 2500ms, TBT <= 200ms, CLS <= 0.1, FCP <= 1500ms
- Resource budgets: JS <= 100KB, total <= 500KB
- Budget violations **fail PR checks**

**Uptime Monitoring** (`.github/workflows/uptime-monitor.yml`)
- Runs every 15 minutes via cron
- Checks backend `/health` and frontend endpoints
- Auto-creates incident issues on downtime, auto-closes on recovery

**Error Tracking** (`frontend/js/error-tracking.js`)
- Lightweight, zero-dependency alternative to Sentry
- Captures: unhandled errors, promise rejections, long tasks, Core Web Vitals
- Buffers and flushes to backend `/api/errors` endpoint

**Performance Improvements**
- Code-split module renderers (esoteric/scientific/realworld chunks)
- Added `perf:budget` script for local budget checking

### Setup Required
- Set `BACKEND_URL` and `FRONTEND_URL` repository variables for uptime monitoring
- Optionally set `LHCI_GITHUB_APP_TOKEN` secret for Lighthouse status checks

Closes #131

body:
## Summary

Backend infrastructure for Phase 04 (Container Management):

- **Lifecycle server actions** (start/stop/shutdown/restart/delete) with Redis-based concurrency locking, Proxmox API integration, and ContainerEvent audit trail
- **ProxmoxClient-from-session helper** — reusable pattern for all authenticated Proxmox operations  
- **DatabaseService extensions** — 7 new query methods (listContainersWithRelations, getContainerCounts, getContainerWithDetails, deleteContainerById, updateContainerServices, createContainerEvent, updateContainerLifecycle)
- **SSH-based service monitoring engine** — checks systemd services, discovers ports via `ss`, reads credentials, and checks config-manager health

### Key Design Decisions

- Redis `SET NX EX 120` lock prevents concurrent lifecycle actions on the same container
- Shutdown has 30s graceful timeout with automatic fallback to force stop  
- Delete stops running containers before removal from both Proxmox and DB
- Monitoring engine is worker-compatible (no `server-only` guard) and returns errors in result object (never throws)
- All server actions use `authActionClient` pattern with `ActionError` for user-facing errors

### Plans

- [x] 04-01: Lifecycle server actions + DB query methods + client helper
- [x] 04-02: Service monitoring engine (SSH-based checks)

| Actions | `src/lib/containers/actions.ts` (extended) |
| DB | `src/lib/db.ts` (extended) |  
| Monitoring | `src/lib/containers/monitoring.ts` |
| Planning | SUMMARY.md files for 04-01, 04-02 |

## Summary

This PR makes `source_interval` and `source_interval_delayed` emit unit values `()` instead of `tokio::time::Instant`, making them deterministic. The `AtLeastOnce` retry type already makes interval sources deterministic semantically, but exposing the `Instant` unnecessarily marked them as non-deterministic.

## Changes

### Modified API
- `source_interval` now returns `Stream<(), Self, Unbounded, TotalOrder, ExactlyOnce>` instead of `Stream<tokio::time::Instant, ...>`
- `source_interval_delayed` now returns `Stream<(), Self, Unbounded, TotalOrder, ExactlyOnce>` instead of `Stream<tokio::time::Instant, ...>`
- Both methods no longer require the `NonDet` parameter since they're now deterministic

### New API
- Added `wall_clock_time(_nondet: NonDet) -> Singleton<tokio::time::Instant, Self, Bounded>` for cases where developers explicitly need access to wall-clock time

## Rationale

This change reduces cognitive burden by focusing `nondet` on situations where the developer explicitly reads wall-clock time, rather than requiring it for all interval-based operations. The interval sources are already deterministic in their event timing semantics (AtLeastOnce), so the non-determinism was only from exposing the arbitrary timestamp values.

## Migration Guide

Before:
```rust
process.source_interval(q!(Duration::from_secs(1)), nondet!(/** explanation */))
    .map(q!(|_instant| do_something()))
```

After:
```rust
process.source_interval(q!(Duration::from_secs(1)))
    .map(q!(|_| do_something()))
```

If you need the wall-clock time:
```rust
tick.wall_clock_time(nondet!(/** explanation */))
    .map(q!(|instant| use_instant(instant)))
```

Fixes #2393

author: copilot
body:
Tag autocomplete dropdown was constrained by parent width (~420px), making long tag names hard to select. Template input dialog used manual lifecycle management instead of DialogManager, lacking ESC support and proper overlay behavior.

## Changes

### Tag Autocomplete Width
- Added `min-width: 250px` to autocomplete dropdown in `createTagInput`
- Ensures sufficient width regardless of parent container constraints

### Template Dialog Refactor
Migrated `createTemplateForm` to DialogManager pattern:

**Before:**
```javascript
const formDialog = createTemplateForm(templates, onSubmit, onCancel);
KeyHandler.isModalOpen = true;
document.body.appendChild(formDialog.overlay);
// Manual cleanup in callbacks
```

**After:**
```javascript
const formDialog = createTemplateForm(templates, onSubmit, onCancel);
// DialogManager handles: registration, ESC key, overlay clicks, cleanup
```

**Implementation:**
- Dialog stack registration via `DialogManager.pushDialog()`
- ESC key handling via `DialogManager.createEscapeHandler()`
- Double-click-to-close via `DialogManager.createOverlayClickHandler()`
- Shadow DOM attachment for proper z-index layering
- Automatic cleanup via `DialogManager.closeDialog()`

Removes manual `KeyHandler.isModalOpen` management and DOM manipulation from call sites.

## Version
Updated to v37 with changelog entry.

body:
### Motivation
- Resolve Dart Sass runtime errors caused by ambiguous variables from globally-injected modules and eliminate deprecated `@import`/helper usage across styles to silence deprecation/runtime issues. 
- Make the manager UI show a faithful, full-page preview of the public `RestaurantDetail` without site chrome for visual validation.

### Description
- Reworked SCSS imports to use the module system (`@use`) and added explicit namespaces for local variable files (notably the RestaurantMenu files import local `variables` as `rm`) to avoid the "variable available from multiple global modules" runtime error. 
- Replaced deprecated built-ins with `sass:` module APIs across many styles, e.g. `darken`/`lighten`/`mix` -> `color.adjust`/`color.mix`, `nth` -> `list.nth`, and `map-get` -> `map.get`, and added `@use "sass:color"`, `@use "sass:list"`, `@use "sass:map"` where needed. 
- Updated `_mixins.scss` to use `color.` helpers and added/adjusted helpers (`custom-darken`/`custom-lighten` now wrap `color.adjust`, `loading-spinner` mixin keyframes fixed) and migrated many `@import` usages to `@use` with appropriate namespaces. 
- Scoped menu-local variables and mixins (files under `src/components/Customer/RestaurantMenu`) to the `rm` namespace and updated all variable/mixin references in those files to `rm.$...` and `@include rm...`. 
- Replaced the compact React preview in `RestaurantInfoManagement.jsx` with an `iframe` that loads `/restaurant/{id}?preview=1` and added responsive iframe sizing and `min-width: 0` styles; updated `MainLayout.jsx` to suppress `Header`/`Footer` when the `preview=1` query parameter is present so embedded previews render without chrome. 
- Miscellaneous: migrated `LoadingSpinner.scss` and many dashboard/manager styles to `@use`, added `@use "sass:color"` to files that call color helpers, and converted various `darken`/`lighten` call sites to `color.adjust` for consistent behavior.

### Testing
- Compiled targeted SCSS files with `npx sass` (using `--load-path src`) to validate `@use` and `sass:` API usage and to catch undefined-import or undeclared-variable errors; files that were tested compiled without the original deprecation/ambiguous-variable errors for the updated targets. (Succeeded for tested files.)
- Searched the codebase with ripgrep to verify `@use`/`sass:` replacements and that plain `nth(`/`@import` usages were removed in the modified paths using patterns like `rg -n "@use \"\./(styles/)?variables\" as (\*|rm);"` and `rg -n "@import|\bnth\("` for the affected directories. (Search validated replacements in the modified files.)
- Started the dev server with `npm run dev` and exercised the customer menu route (`/cus-menu`) and the manager preview route to trigger Vite/Sass compilation; confirmed the previously reported Sass ambiguity errors for RestaurantMenu no longer appear in Vite logs and captured a screenshot of `/cus-menu` to validate runtime rendering. (Dev server started; RestaurantMenu Sass ambiguity errors resolved.)
- Note: unrelated import-resolution errors still surface in the app (missing legacy `./styles/globals.scss` and other missing style imports) that are outside the scoped fixes in this PR and remain to be addressed separately.

author: sahearn1
body:
## Summary

Implements a comprehensive Non-Violent Communication (NVC) quality assurance system that evaluates AI tutor responses for compliance with trauma-informed pedagogy principles. This system automatically flags responses containing judgmental language, dismissive tone, or other NVC violations, enabling educators to review and improve the quality of AI-generated feedback.

## Key Changes

- **Database Schema**: Added `NVCQualityEvaluation` model with comprehensive evaluation tracking including compliance scores, identified concerns, suggested revisions, and admin review workflow
- **NVC Evaluator**: Implemented `evaluateNVCCompliance()` function using Claude Haiku to analyze responses against 10 NVC violation categories (judgmental language, dismissive tone, lack of empathy, authoritarian language, shaming, comparison, demands vs requests, diagnosis vs observation, blame, and coercive language)
- **Evaluation Service**: Created service layer with functions to:
  - Create evaluations and store results in database
  - Retrieve pending and flagged evaluations for admin review
  - Update review status with admin actions
  - Generate statistics and analytics on NVC compliance trends
- **Admin API Endpoints**: Added three new endpoints:
  - `GET /api/admin/nvc-evaluations` - List evaluations with filtering (pending/flagged)
  - `GET /api/admin/nvc-evaluations/[id]` - Retrieve specific evaluation details
  - `PATCH /api/admin/nvc-evaluations/[id]` - Update review status and admin actions
  - `GET /api/admin/nvc-evaluations/stats` - Get compliance statistics
- **Chat Integration**: Modified chat endpoint to asynchronously trigger NVC evaluation for all assistant responses without blocking the response stream
- **Comprehensive Tests**: Added 649 lines of test coverage for both the evaluator and service layer with mocked LLM calls and database operations

## Implementation Details

- **Async Evaluation**: NVC evaluation runs asynchronously after response is sent to user, preventing latency impact
- **Automatic Routing**: Compliant responses (score ≥80) are auto-approved; non-compliant responses enter PENDING review status
- **Batch Processing**: Supports batch evaluation of multiple responses with configurable concurrency limits
- **Tenant Isolation**: All evaluations are scoped to tenant with proper authorization checks
- **Cost Optimization**: Uses Claude Haiku (lightweight model) for evaluations to minimize API costs
- **Detailed Analysis**: Captures specific problematic phrases, suggested revisions, token usage, and latency metrics for each evaluation

## Admin Workflow

1. System automatically evaluates all assistant responses
2. Non-compliant responses appear in admin dashboard for review
3. Educators can approve, flag, dismiss, or take corrective actions
4. Actions tracked with timestamps and notes for audit trail
5. Statistics dashboard shows compliance trends and top concerns

## Summary

- Cache Pester + PSScriptAnalyzer modules using `actions/cache@v4` in test.yml (4 jobs) and pssa.yml (1 job)
- Skip `Install-Module` entirely on cache hit
- Cache key per OS + shell type with manual version suffix (`v1`) for forced invalidation

## Expected impact

| Job | Before | After (cached) | Saved |
|-----|--------|----------------|-------|
| Ubuntu PS 7 | 14s install | ~2s restore | ~12s |
| macOS PS 7 | 13s install | ~2s restore | ~11s |
| Windows PS 7 | 34s install | ~3s restore | ~31s |
| **Windows PS 5.1** | **180s install** | **~3s restore** | **~177s** |
| PSSA lint | 10s install | ~2s restore | ~8s |

First run per cache key will be normal speed (cache miss → install → save). Subsequent runs restore from cache.

## Cache invalidation

Bump the version suffix in the cache key (`v1` → `v2`) to force fresh module installation. GitHub also auto-evicts caches unused for 7 days.

## Test plan

- [ ] First CI run: cache miss, installs normally, saves cache
- [ ] Verify all 4 test jobs + PSSA lint pass
- [ ] Subsequent runs should show cache hit and skip Install-Module steps

### Motivation
- Improve the Daily Net chart tooltip to surface the primary metric first (`Net`) and make prior-period comparisons more informative by showing a signed delta and percent change when appropriate.
- Avoid noisy or malformed strings by normalizing null/undefined/zero inputs and keeping formatting robust for edge cases.
- Increase tooltip legibility by tuning spacing and typography so the primary metric has stronger contrast.

### Description
- Refactored tooltip construction in `frontend/src/components/charts/DailyNetChart.vue` by changing `buildTooltipLines()` to render `Net` first, then `Income`, `Expenses`, and `Transactions`, and to normalize numeric inputs before formatting.
- Added comparison summary logic that emits a `vs prior` line with signed currency delta and a percent change when the comparison baseline is non-zero, and suppresses noisy percent text when the baseline is zero or invalid.
- Tuned Chart.js tooltip options for spacing and typography (explicit `padding`, `titleFont`/`bodyFont` size/weight, and `bodySpacing`) so the primary metric reads with stronger contrast.
- Updated unit/component tests and docs: modified `frontend/src/components/charts/__tests__/DailyNetChart.spec.js` to cover net-first ordering, comparison delta formatting, and zero-baseline behavior; and updated `docs/devnotes/daily-net-chart.md` to document the new tooltip order and comparison summary.

author: artoo-claw
body:
## Problem
The token selector shows no tokens because:
1. The common tokens hook tries to enrich static token data via Uniswap GQL backend
2. GQL fails for LightLink (not a supported chain)
3. Enriched data comes back `undefined`, making the COMMON_BASES fallback useless
4. Token list stays in loading state or shows empty

## Fix
When GQL enrichment fails, fall back directly to static `COMMON_BASES` token options. Also sets `loading=false` when using fallback to prevent infinite loading spinner.

Combined with the API fix (PR #5 on uniswap-API adding `project` field to swappable_tokens), this should make the token selector work.

author: luckythecookie
body:
## Summary

Implements settings lock protection for Dragon Launcher (#81).

### Features
- **PIN Code**: Set a 4+ digit PIN to protect access to advanced settings
- **Biometric (Fingerprint)**: Use device fingerprint to unlock settings
- **Device Credentials**: Use Android pattern/PIN/password to unlock settings
- **Session-based unlock**: Once authenticated, settings stay accessible until you leave the settings screen

### Implementation Details
- `LockMethod` enum in `core/enumsui`
- `lockMethod` setting in `BehaviorSettingsStore` (backed up with settings)
- `lockPinHash` in `PrivateSettingsStore` (SHA-256, NOT backed up for security)
- Lock gate in `SettingsNavHost` intercepts navigation to advanced settings
- Lock method picker dialog in `AdvancedSettingsScreen`
- `PinDialogs.kt`: PIN unlock dialog + PIN setup dialog (enter + confirm)
- `SecurityHelper.kt`: PIN hashing, BiometricPrompt wrappers, availability checks
- Added `androidx.biometric:biometric:1.1.0` dependency

### UI Flow
1. User goes to Advanced Settings → Lock Settings section
2. Selects a lock method (None / PIN / Fingerprint / Device Credentials)
3. If PIN: enter + confirm PIN dialog
4. Next time accessing Advanced Settings: authentication is required
5. Once unlocked, stays unlocked for the session

### Test Plan
- Set PIN lock → leave settings → re-enter → verify PIN dialog appears
- Set biometric lock → verify fingerprint prompt appears
- Set device credentials → verify Android lock screen prompt appears
- Set to None → verify no prompt
- Wrong PIN → verify error message

Closes #81

author: decklanorie
body:
… on simulator.

[FIX] Remove AVMutableVideoComposition as it was causing black screen on simulator. The main objective of AVMutableVideoComposition was to prevent black screen on physical devices by correcting the tranform of the video track, probably it is not required anymore as we are using UIView with AVPlayerLayer instead of textures. This commit removes the change of video track transform for both physical device and iOS simulator, taking the assumption that the change of transform was only required by AVPlayerItemOutput.

author: copilot
body:
Deployment fails because Cloudflare cannot pull `ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:latest`. Remove container configuration to allow standard Worker deployment.

## Changes

**wrangler.jsonc:**
- Remove `containers` array referencing ghcr.io image
- Remove `durable_objects.bindings` for Sandbox class
- Remove `migrations` for Sandbox SQLite class

## Runtime Behavior

Worker deploys successfully but will fail at runtime when accessing sandbox functionality. The code still imports `@cloudflare/sandbox` and expects `c.env.Sandbox` binding. This is a deployment fix only - full functionality requires either:
- Image registry access restored
- Code refactored to remove container dependency
- Alternative container deployment strategy

## Secrets

`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` remains documented in wrangler.jsonc line 83.

author: caetanojpo
body:
* 🎯 **What:** Removed the `token` property from `LoginResponse` and `ConfirmRegistrationResponse` interfaces and implemented logic in `authApi.login` and `authApi.confirmRegistration` to strip the token from the API response before returning it to the caller.
* ⚠️ **Risk:** Although HttpOnly cookies are used for authentication, the backend was still returning the token in the response body. If this token were stored in client-side state (e.g., React Query cache), it could be accessible to XSS attacks.
* 🛡️ **Solution:** By stripping the token at the API layer, we ensure it never reaches the application state, reducing the attack surface. Added tests to verify this behavior.

---
