author: stewartmoreland
body:
## Summary

Refactors the chat UI so messages, thinking blocks, and tool executions render in a **single chronological sequence** (like Cursor / v0), instead of separate sections. Introduces a **`TranscriptItem`** union type and an **`items`**-based API so the transcript can be built and rendered sequentially from a flat event stream.

## Motivation

- **Inline, chronological order**: Users see thinking and tool calls interleaved with assistant message chunks in the order they occur, instead of messages first, then a thinking block, then a tools section.
- **Single source of truth**: One ordered list drives the whole transcript; the UI no longer has to reconcile separate `messages`, `thinkingContent`, and `toolExecutions` arrays.
- **Streaming-friendly**: As events arrive (e.g. `thinking.delta`, `tool.start`, `message.delta`), we append or update items in place and re-render the same list.

## Changes

### `packages/ui` – ChatTranscript & TranscriptItem

- **`TranscriptItem` union**  
  - `MessageItem` (`kind: 'message'`), `ThinkingItem` (`kind: 'thinking'`), `ToolCallItem` (`kind: 'tool'`).  
  - Enables a single ordered array of items and a single render pass with a `switch (item.kind)`.

- **`ChatTranscript` API**  
  - **Primary**: `items?: TranscriptItem[]` — ordered list of items to render in sequence.  
  - **Legacy**: `messages`, `streamingMessageId`, `thinkingContent`, `isThinkingStreaming`, `toolExecutions` remain supported; if `items` is provided, it takes priority and the component builds from it. Otherwise it builds the same list from the legacy props (messages → thinking → tools) for backward compatibility.

- **Rendering**  
  - One list: `resolvedItems.map(item => ...)` with a switch that renders `ChatMessage`, `ThinkingAccordion`, or `ToolCallAccordion` by `item.kind`.  
  - All items render inline in document order with the same layout (e.g. thinking/tools with `pl-9 sm:pl-12`).

- **Exports**  
  - `TranscriptItem`, `MessageItem`, `ThinkingItem`, `ToolCallItem` (and existing `Message`, `ToolExecution`) so consumers can build and pass `items`.

### `apps/web` – App.tsx

- **Event stream → `transcriptItems`**  
  - New `useMemo` that processes the flat `events` array (from `useAgentStream`) into `transcriptItems: TranscriptItem[]`.  
  - Splits events by run boundary (`isRunStartEvent`), then walks each segment in chronological order:  
    - `thinking.delta` → create or update a `ThinkingItem`, append to list.  
    - `tool.start` → create `ToolExecution`, push `ToolCallItem`.  
    - `tool.end` → update existing tool’s `output`, `status`, `endTime`.  
    - `message.delta` → create or update a `MessageItem` (assistant), append/update in list.  
  - Result: one array where thinking blocks and tool calls appear **between** message chunks in time order.

- **Building the full transcript**  
  - `allItems`: merges (1) session history as `MessageItem[]`, (2) user messages + run-specific `transcriptItems` so each user message is followed by that run’s thinking/tools/assistant items, (3) any remaining transcript items (e.g. current stream).  
  - Single ordered list passed to the transcript: `<ChatTranscript items={allItems} />`.

- **Derived state**  
  - `allMessages` is derived from `allItems` (filter `kind === 'message'`, map to `message`) for the header message count.  
  - No separate state for “messages” vs “thinking” vs “tools”; the transcript is driven entirely by `allItems`.

## Backward compatibility

- Existing call sites that pass only `messages`, `streamingMessageId`, `thinkingContent`, `isThinkingStreaming`, and `toolExecutions` continue to work: `ChatTranscript` builds the same ordered list internally when `items` is not provided.

## Testing

- Manual: run a chat, trigger thinking and tool calls; confirm order is chronological (thinking → tools → message chunks) and that streaming updates the same items in place.
- Any existing tests that use the legacy props should still pass; new tests can use `items` for more precise control.

author: gardenwalk
body:
Summary: Adds a development env flag that uses manage_channels in dev instead of manage_events so the dev server can restrict access w/o granting everyone manage_events.

Closes #64 

Major changes:

- There's a couple new globals (is_development, admin_permission, admin_permission_attr) derived from existing env config

- All @app_commands.default_permissions(manage_events=True) decorators across bot command files now unpack 'admin_permission' instead of hardcoding the permission

- users.py resolved_permissions check uses getattr w/ admin_permission_attr instead of accessing manage_events

- All changes are just mechanical replacements of the hardcoded permission with the new global except for getattr which is necessary b/c attribute access can't be dynamic with dot notation

Non-obvious change:
The only non-obvious change is adding Claude.md to the gitignore which helps LLMs read through codebases faster locally

Testing:
pytest passes, behavior difference only noticable when environment = dev in config.toml, which switches required permission from manage_events to manage_channels. I didn't test it by signing in with Google, not 100% if I should sign in with another email besides the main cybersecurity club email given it sends out emails/looks at calendar

Impact awareness:
- No breaking changes in prod b/c it only affects dev
- Dev server members will need manage_channels instead of manage_events to use admin commands

author: armatis
body:
## Summary

New puzzle game mode where players launch satellites from one orbit to be captured by another. Based on real orbital mechanics - satellites launch tangentially when gravity is released.

## Gameplay

- **Multiple attractors** with orbiting satellites
- **Charge mechanic**: Hold mousedown on attractor to speed up orbiting satellites
- **Launch**: Release to let satellites fly tangentially with their current velocity
- **Capture**: Satellites get pulled into another attractor's gravity well
- **Win condition**: Get satellite from start orbit to target orbit

## Features

- 5 progressive levels with increasing complexity
- Visual feedback for charging (orange intensity, charge arc indicator)
- Target attractor has pulsing green glow
- Capture radius shown as subtle dashed circles
- Launch counter per level
- Reset and Next Level buttons

## Level Progression

1. Simple two-attractor straight shot
2. Angled trajectory
3. Relay through middle attractor
4. Two possible paths
5. Triangle relay with 2 satellites

## Test plan

- [ ] Switch to Orbital mode in Games tab
- [ ] Start Level 1
- [ ] Hold on the left attractor (with satellite) to charge
- [ ] Release when satellite is aimed at target
- [ ] Verify satellite flies tangentially
- [ ] Verify capture when entering target's radius
- [ ] Verify level complete message
- [ ] Test Next Level progression
- [ ] Test Reset Level
- [ ] Verify mode switching cleans up properly

body:
Establishes Python/FastAPI backend structure with type-safe configuration management, adapting patterns from the prototype at `hdayplanner/` (now archived).

## Structure

Created modular package layout:
- `app/config/` - Pydantic Settings with validation and startup logging
- `app/api/` - Route handlers (empty, ready for Phase 2)
- `app/services/` - Business logic layer (empty, ready for Phase 2)
- `app/audit/` - Audit logging (empty, ready for Phase 2)

## Configuration

`app/config/settings.py` implements environment-based config with Pydantic field validators:

```python
from app.config import settings

# Validates environment mode, creates SHARE_DIR automatically
settings.ensure_share_dir_exists()

# Parses comma-separated origins, rejects wildcards in production
cors_origins = settings.get_cors_origins_list()
```

Configuration variables: `SHARE_DIR`, `CORS_ORIGINS`, `ENVIRONMENT`, `HOST`, `PORT`, `CACHE_TTL`, `CACHE_ENABLED`

## Application

`app/main.py` provides FastAPI app with:
- Lifespan context manager for startup/shutdown hooks
- CORS middleware with production-safe validation
- Health check endpoint (`/healthz`)
- Auto-generated OpenAPI documentation

## Testing

18 tests (12 config validation, 6 endpoint integration) covering:
- Environment variable parsing and overrides
- CORS origin validation (single, multiple, wildcard handling)
- Production/development mode differences
- Share directory creation with permission error handling
- API endpoints and documentation

## Dependencies

`requirements.txt`: FastAPI >=0.128.0, Uvicorn >=0.40.0, Pydantic >=2.12.0, pydantic-settings >=2.0.0, python-dotenv >=1.2.0

Prototype preserved at `hdayplanner.archived/` for reference.

body:
## Summary

- Listen to xterm.js `onTitleChange` in `TerminalPane` so programs that set the terminal title via OSC escape sequences (e.g. `\x1b]0;title\x07`) update the tab name — matching Windows Terminal behavior
- Add `oscTitle` field to `Terminal` store with display priority: user rename > OSC title > process name
- Clear `oscTitle` when the process monitor detects a process change, preventing stale titles after exiting a program
- Fix `OpenProcess` flags in process monitor to include `PROCESS_VM_READ` for more reliable process name detection

## Test plan

- [x] 5 new store tests covering oscTitle storage, clearing, preservation, and multi-terminal isolation
- [x] All 136 TypeScript tests pass
- [x] Rust crates compile cleanly (`cargo check -p godly-protocol -p godly-daemon`)
- [x] Production build succeeds (`npm run build`)
- [ ] Manual: run Claude Code in a terminal tab and verify the tab name updates to reflect Claude's title
- [ ] Manual: exit Claude Code and verify the tab name reverts to the shell process name

author: copilot
body:
Restructures the codebase to enable shared code compilation for both kernel and userspace targets. Kernel-specific code moves to `master/kernel/`, userspace-specific code to `master/uspace/`, shared code remains in `master/`.

## Directory Structure

```
master/
├── (shared PAL-compatible code)
├── kernel/          # Kernel-specific: device, cdev, module, ioctl, rtdm
│   └── pal.h        # Kernel PAL (Linux APIs)
└── uspace/          # Userspace-specific: daemon, transport
    └── pal.h        # Userspace PAL (POSIX APIs)
```

**Migrated to `master/kernel/`:**
- Device layer: `device.c/h`, `cdev.c/h`, `module.c`, `debug.c/h`
- ioctl handling: `ioctl.c/h`, `rtdm*.c/h`
- `pal_kernel.c` → `kernel/pal.c`

**Migrated to `master/uspace/`:**
- `userspace/pal_user.c` → `uspace/pal.c`
- `userspace/ethercat_master.c`, `userspace/transport/`
- `userspace/list.h` → `uspace/list.h`

## PAL Header Split

Replaced monolithic `master/pal.h` with platform-specific headers using include path switching:

**Kernel:** `-I$(src)/kernel` → `#include "pal.h"` finds `kernel/pal.h`
```c
// kernel/pal.h
#define ec_pal_malloc(size)    kmalloc(size, GFP_KERNEL)
#define ec_pal_jiffies()       jiffies
```

**Userspace:** `-I$(srcdir)` → `#include "pal.h"` finds `uspace/pal.h`
```c
// uspace/pal.h
#define ec_pal_malloc(size)    malloc(size)
static inline unsigned long ec_pal_jiffies(void) {
    struct timespec ts;
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &ts);
    return ts.tv_sec * 1000 + ts.tv_nsec / 1000000;
}
```

## Build System Changes

- **Kbuild:** Updated object paths with `kernel/` prefix, added `-I$(src)/kernel` to `ccflags-y`
- **Autotools:** Moved `userspace/Makefile` → `master/uspace/Makefile` in `configure.ac`
- **Include paths:** Fixed all references in moved files (`../master.h`, `../../devices/ecdev.h`)
- **Tool/lib:** Updated ioctl.h references to `master/kernel/ioctl.h`

Shared headers now reference `"uspace/list.h"` for userspace list compatibility layer.

# Phase 1: Restructure directories for kernel/userspace code separation

This PR implements Phase 1 of the kernel/userspace code separation as documented in `documentation/SPLIT_USER_KERNEL.md`.

## Goal

Restructure the directory layout to separate kernel-specific and userspace-specific code, enabling shared code to be compiled for both targets using include path switching.

## Target Directory Structure

```
master/
├── (shared .c/.h files remain here)
├── kernel/                    # KERNEL-SPECIFIC
│   ├── pal.h                  # Kernel PAL definitions
│   ├── pal.c                  # Kernel PAL implementation
│   ├── device.c, device.h     # Kernel device using sk_buff
│   ├── cdev.c, cdev.h         # Character device
│   ├── module.c               # Module init/exit
│   ├── debug.c, debug.h       # Debug network interface
│   ├── ioctl.c, ioctl.h       # ioctl handling
│   ├── rtdm*.c/h              # RTDM support
│   └── ...
│
└── uspace/                    # USERSPACE-SPECIFIC
    ├── pal.h                  # Userspace PAL definitions
    ├── pal.c                  # Userspace PAL implementation  
    ├── device.c               # Userspace device using transport
    ├── ecrt_user.c/h          # Userspace API extensions
    ├── ethercat_master.c      # Standalone daemon
    ├── Makefile.am
    └── transport/             # Transport layer
        ├── ec_transport.h
        ├── transport.c
        └── transport_raw.c
```

## Files to Move

### To `master/kernel/`:

From `master/`:
- `device.c` → `master/kernel/device.c`
- `device.h` → `master/kernel/device.h`
- `cdev.c` → `master/kernel/cdev.c`
- `cdev.h` → `master/kernel/cdev.h`
- `module.c` → `master/kernel/module.c`
- `debug.c` → `master/kernel/debug.c`
- `debug.h` → `master/kernel/debug.h`
- `ioctl.c` → `master/kernel/ioctl.c`
- `ioctl.h` → `master/kernel/ioctl.h`
- `rtdm.c` → `master/kernel/rtdm.c`
- `rtdm.h` → `master/kernel/rtdm.h`
- `rtdm-ioctl.c` → `master/kernel/rtdm-ioctl.c`
- `rtdm_details.h` → `master/kernel/rtdm_details.h`
- `rtdm_xenomai_v3.c` → `master/kernel/rtdm_xenomai_v3.c`
- `pal_kernel.c` → `master/kernel/pal.c` (rename)

### To `master/uspace/`:

From `userspace/`:
- `pal_user.c` → `master/uspace/pal.c` (rename)
- `ecrt_user.c` → `master/uspace/ecrt_user.c`
- `ethercat_master.c` → `master/uspace/ethercat_master.c`
- `Makefile.am` → `master/uspace/Makefile.am`
- `include/ecrt_user.h` → `master/uspace/ecrt_user.h`
- `transport/` → `master/uspace/transport/` (entire directory)
  - `ec_transport.h`
  - `transport.c`
  - `transport_raw.c`

## Files to Create

### `master/kernel/pal.h`
New kernel PAL header with:
- Kernel includes (`<linux/types.h>`, `<linux/spinlock.h>`, etc.)
- `ec_device_plat_t` definition (kernel-specific device fields)
- `ec_master_plat_t` definition (kernel-specific master fields)
- Access macros: `ec_master_lock()`, `ec_device_lock()`, etc.
- Logging macros: `EC_MASTER_INFO()`, `EC_MASTER_ERR()`, etc.
- Time macros: `ec_time_t`, `ec_time_now()`, `ec_time_after()`, etc.
- Memory macros: `ec_malloc()`, `ec_zalloc()`, `ec_free()`

### `master/uspace/pal.h`
New userspace PAL header with:
- Userspace includes (`<stdint.h>`, `<pthread.h>`, etc.)
- `ec_device_plat_t` definition (with `ec_transport_t *`)
- `ec_master_plat_t` definition (with pthread types)
- Same access macros but with userspace implementations
- Same logging macros using `fprintf(stderr, ...)`
- Same time macros using `clock_gettime()`
- Same memory macros using `malloc()`/`free()`

### `master/uspace/device.c`
New userspace device implementation:
- `ec_device_init()` - initialize device
- `ec_device_clear()` - cleanup device
- `ec_device_open()` - open transport
- `ec_device_close()` - close transport
- `ec_device_tx_data()` - get TX buffer from transport
- `ec_device_send()` - send via transport
- `ec_device_poll()` - poll for received frames
- `ec_device_get_link()` - get link state
- `ec_device_clear_stats()` - clear statistics

## Files to Delete

- `master/pal.h` - no longer needed (include path switching handles this)
- `userspace/` directory - after moving all contents to `master/uspace/`

## Build System Updates

### `master/Kbuild.in`
- Add `-I$(src)/kernel` to `ccflags-y`
- Update object file paths to include `kernel/` prefix for moved files:
  ```makefile
  ec_master-objs := \
      kernel/device.o \
      kernel/cdev.o \
      kernel/module.o \
      kernel/debug.o \
      kernel/ioctl.o \
      kernel/pal.o \
      # ... kernel objects with kernel/ prefix
      master.o \
      slave.o \
      # ... shared objects without prefix
  ```

### `master/uspace/Makefile.am`
- Update include paths: `-I$(srcdir)` (finds uspace/pal.h)
- Add `-I$(top_srcdir)/master` for shared headers
- Update source file paths for moved files
- Reference shared sources from parent directory

### `configure.ac`
- Change `userspace/Makefile` to `master/uspace/Makefile` in `AC_CONFIG_FILES`

### Top-level `Makefile.am`
- Remove `userspace` from `SUBDIRS` if presen...
